memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"After Moses had sent away his wife Zipporah, his father-in-law Jethro received
her and her two sons. One son was named Gershom, for Moses said, 'I have become
a foreigner in a foreign land'; and the other was named Eliezer, for he said,
'My father's God was my helper; he saved me from the sword of Pharaoh.'"
- Ex 18:2-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two boys, two names, and together they tell the story of Moses' life.

Gershom means "a foreigner there." Moses named his firstborn out of his sense of
displacement. He had lost Egypt, lost his position, and was living in a land not
his own. That name is honest. It records a season of loneliness.

Eliezer means "my God is helper." By the time the second son was born, Moses
could name a child after God's rescue rather than his own dislocation.

Notice that both names stand. Scripture does not erase the first one. The season
of feeling like a foreigner was real, and Moses did not pretend otherwise.

Many of us have a Gershom season in our history, a stretch where we felt out of
place and unsure whether we belonged anywhere. It is honest to name it. And many
of us can also, later, name an Eliezer, a point where we could say God helped
us.

Notice too the quiet detail that Zipporah and the boys had been sent away. Moses'
family life carried strain. Scripture does not tidy this up or explain it. Even
faithful servants of God have complicated households.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What would you name the season you are currently in?
2. Can you look back and honestly say "God was my helper"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You have been my helper even in the seasons when I felt like a stranger.
Thank You for holding me through both. Amen.
